skill.name: baoyu-cover-image
skill.description: Generate article cover images by combining content type, palette, rendering style, text density, mood, font, and aspect ratio options.
skill.summary: A guided workflow for creating consistent, article-ready cover images with selectable visual dimensions and raster image backends.
skill.author: JimLiu

remediation.issue: Static analysis interprets Markdown backticks and command examples as executable shell usage.
remediation.suggestion: Keep backend commands clearly labeled as examples and place executable implementation in reviewed, separately scanned scripts.

remediation.issue: Configuration and cache paths under hidden home directories trigger filesystem alerts.
remediation.suggestion: Document that these paths are user-selected preferences and caches, and restrict writes to the skill-specific directories.

remediation.issue: Relative documentation links and the repository homepage trigger path and network heuristics.
remediation.suggestion: Preserve the links, but state that they are documentation-only and that runtime network access belongs to the selected image backend.

content.value_statement: Article creators need consistent cover visuals without manually designing every composition. This skill guides image prompts across style, color, layout, text, mood, and aspect ratio choices.
actual_capabilities: Generate structured prompts for article cover images.
Choose among six cover types, eleven palettes, and seven rendering styles.
Control title density, mood, font style, language, and aspect ratio.
Use source content and reference images to guide visual composition.
Save prompts and generated assets in organized topic-based output directories.
limitations: Requires an available raster image-generation backend.
Does not guarantee perfect lettering or typography in generated images.
Does not edit bitmap text after generation; corrections require regeneration.
Backend availability, output quality, and model capabilities vary by runtime.

use_cases.title: Create a Blog Header
use_cases.description: Turn an article title and short summary into a balanced cover prompt with a suitable visual metaphor and aspect ratio.

use_cases.title: Standardize Editorial Branding
use_cases.description: Apply repeatable palettes, rendering styles, fonts, and watermark preferences across a publication library.

use_cases.title: Prepare Social Variants
use_cases.description: Generate square, portrait, widescreen, or cinematic cover directions for different publishing channels.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Cover
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a clean article cover for [title]. Use a single visual metaphor, balanced mood, title-only text, and a 16:9 aspect ratio.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: one title with default visual choices

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Visual Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [type] cover for [title]. Use the [palette] palette, [rendering] rendering, [font] font, title-subtitle text, and [aspect] aspect ratio. Keep the composition uncluttered.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: explicit style and layout controls

prompt_templates.title: Match Source Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this article summary: [summary]. Extract its topic, tone, and keywords, then create a cover prompt using a relevant metaphor, suitable palette, rendering style, mood, language, and aspect ratio.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Reference-Led Cover
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the provided reference image for visual direction. Preserve its key composition, palette behavior, and typography hierarchy while creating an original cover for [title]. Specify the required elements, placement, text level, and [aspect] aspect ratio.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: reference-guided composition with reproducible prompt output

output_examples.input: Article: Practical API security for small teams. Style: cool flat-vector, title-only, 16:9.
output_examples.output: A structured cover prompt featuring a simplified lock, API brackets, and connected service nodes. The design uses a cool technical palette, clear whitespace, and a large exact title.

output_examples.input: Article: A quiet guide to focused work. Style: minimal, warm, painterly, square.
output: A single desk lamp beside a short written title, with generous calm space.
Warm restrained colors, soft painterly edges, balanced contrast, and a square composition.

best_practices: Provide the exact article title and a concise content summary.
Confirm the six visual dimensions before generation unless quick mode is explicitly requested.
Keep each final prompt in a standalone file so the result can be reproduced or regenerated.
anti_patterns: Do not invent or alter the source title in the generated cover prompt.
Do not replace raster generation with SVG, HTML, canvas, or other code-based artwork.
Do not paint over incorrect bitmap text; regenerate with a corrected prompt instead.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It creates prompts and workflow guidance for article cover images in several layouts, palettes, renderings, text levels, and moods.

faq.question: Which aspect ratios are supported?
faq.answer: It supports 16:9, 2.35:1, 4:3, 3:2, 1:1, and 3:4, with 16:9 as the default.

faq.question: Can I use a reference image?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow can save reference images, describe their visual traits, and pass compatible references to the selected backend.

faq.question: Does it add text after generation?
faq.answer: No. It keeps text correction inside the image-generation workflow and requires regeneration when lettering is incorrect.

faq.question: Does it require a specific image backend?
faq.answer: No. It selects an available native or installed raster backend according to the current runtime and saved preferences.

faq.question: What is quick mode?
faq.answer: Quick mode skips most dimension confirmation and uses automatic selections. The aspect ratio is still confirmed unless explicitly specified.
